# Two Estimates of the 1906 Earthquake

Two approaches produced different estimates of the 1906 earthquake’s magnitude. A seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7, while a USGS team’s re-evaluation of geodetic measurements estimated 7.9.

The seismic analysis examined recordings from 96 observatories. It digitized and modeled usable data from 12 of them, yielding the 7.7 estimate.

The USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake. These measurements captured ground deformation through changes in angles and distances between benchmarks, and the analysis produced an estimate of 7.9.

The estimates came from different kinds of measurements, illustrating that methods for estimating earthquake size can yield different results.
